issues.t: Ignition switch can slip out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off without warning while driving, often after a bump or when your knee brushes a heavy key ring. Steering and brakes suddenly take much more effort.
issues.why: The ignition switch was built with too little turning resistance, so the key can be knocked from Run to Accessory. That stops the engine and can keep the airbags from deploying in a crash. GM recall 14V-047 replaces the switch.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 14V-047 right away. Until it is done, carry only the ignition key on the ring with nothing hanging from it.

issues.t: Power steering assist cuts out (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly gets very heavy, mostly at low speeds and while parking, and a power steering warning may appear. It can come and go.
issues.why: The electric power steering motor can stop working when worn brush material and oily debris build up inside it. NHTSA opened an investigation on 2004-2007 Ions, and GM recall 14V-153 later covered these cars.
issues.next: You can still steer, it just takes more muscle, so slow down and grip the wheel firmly. Check your VIN for open recall 14V-153.

issues.t: VTi CVT transmission slips or fails
issues.sym: The car revs but does not pick up speed, jerks, makes loud whining or grinding noises, or will not move in Drive or Reverse.
issues.why: Automatic 2003-2004 Ions used GM's VTi continuously variable transmission (CVT), which had a high failure rate. GM extended its warranty and later settled a class action lawsuit over it.
issues.next: Stop driving hard if it slips. Get a transmission diagnosis; most failed units are replaced rather than repaired. Keep your repair receipts.

issues.t: Key can come out when not in Off (recall)
issues.sym: You can pull the key out even though the ignition is not fully turned to Off.
issues.why: Wear in the ignition lock cylinder lets the key come out too early. On an automatic the car may not be locked in Park and could roll away. GM recall 14V-171 fixes the lock cylinder.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake when you park. Check your VIN for open recall 14V-171.

issues.t: Fuel pump module can crack and leak gas (recall)
issues.sym: A strong gas smell around the car or inside it, sometimes with hard starting.
issues.why: The plastic fuel pump module on top of the gas tank can crack and leak fuel, which is a fire risk. GM recalls 09V-419 and 12V-459 cover the module.
issues.next: If you smell gas, do not drive it or park it in a garage. Check your VIN for open recalls 09V-419 and 12V-459.

issues.t: Key stuck in ignition or engine won't shut off
issues.sym: The key will not turn back to Off or will not come out, and sometimes the engine keeps running with the key stuck.
issues.why: The ignition will only release the key when the shifter tells it the car is in Park. A worn shifter park switch, shift cable or ignition lock cylinder breaks that signal.
issues.next: Move the shifter firmly into Park and try again. A shop can test the park switch and lock cylinder; one of those is usually replaced.

issues.t: Intermittent no-crank or no-start
issues.sym: Some days you turn the key and nothing happens, or the engine cranks but does not start. Then it starts fine later.
issues.why: Owners trace this to a worn ignition switch or its wiring. A weak battery connection or a fault in the anti-theft system can cause the same symptom.
issues.next: Note whether the dash lights come on and whether the engine cranks; that helps a shop find it. Ask them to check the ignition switch and its connector first.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle and tensioner failure
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine at cold start or idle, a check engine light for cam timing codes such as P0016, rough running, or in the worst case a no-start.
issues.why: The timing chain tensioner and guides wear out, and on early 2.2L engines the tensioner did not get enough oil at idle. Low or old oil speeds it up and lets the chain stretch.
issues.next: Keep the oil full and changed on time. If you hear the rattle or get timing codes, have the chain, guides and tensioner replaced before the chain jumps a tooth and damages the engine.

issues.t: Intake manifold gasket leak
issues.sym: Rough idle, misfires, weak acceleration, a check engine light, and sometimes a milky residue under the oil cap.
issues.why: The intake manifold gasket on the early Ecotec 2.2L is a known weak spot and can leak air or coolant as it ages.
issues.next: Have a shop smoke-test for vacuum leaks and check for coolant loss. Replacing the gasket is a modest job if done before other damage.

issues.t: Coolant loss from a cracked cylinder head
issues.sym: Coolant keeps disappearing, the engine runs hot, white smoke comes from the tailpipe, or oil looks milky.
issues.why: Owners of 2004 Ions report cracked cylinder heads, usually found while chasing coolant loss or overheating.
issues.next: Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs. Ask for a cooling-system pressure test and a combustion gas test before deciding whether a head or engine swap makes sense.

issues.t: Fuel filter can corrode and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or drips of fuel under the car near the fuel filter.
issues.why: The outer shell of the fuel filter can rust through and leak gas, which could catch fire. GM recall 04V-003 replaces the filter.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park it outside and check your VIN for open recall 04V-003.

issues.t: Front turn signal may not work (recall)
issues.sym: A front turn signal does not flash, or the dash signal flashes fast.
issues.why: The bulb design shared by the front turn signal and daytime running light could stop the turn signal from working. GM recall 04V-547 fixes it.
issues.next: Check your turn signals by walking around the car. Check your VIN for open recall 04V-547.

issues.t: Power window and sunroof switches miss child-safety rule (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom; the windows and sunroof work normally.
issues.why: The power window and sunroof switches did not meet the federal rule meant to stop a child from closing a window on themselves by accident. GM recall 04V-004 changed the switches.
issues.next: Never leave children alone in the car with the key in it. Check your VIN for open recall 04V-004.

issues.t: Power windows stop working
issues.sym: A window will not go up or down, moves slowly, or drops into the door.
issues.why: The window regulator or motor wears out, and a worn switch can also stop a window.
issues.next: Keep the window closed if you can and tape it up if it drops. A shop can tell whether the switch, motor or regulator failed.

issues.t: Sunroof leak
issues.sym: Water drips from the headliner, the front pillars or onto the floor after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: The sunroof tray drains clog with dirt or come loose, so water overflows into the cabin.
issues.next: Clear the drain tubes at the sunroof corners. If water still comes in, have the drain hoses checked and reattached.

issues.t: Misfire from ignition coil or module failure
issues.sym: The engine shakes or stumbles, loses power, and the check engine light may flash.
issues.why: The ignition coil pack (ignition module) that fires the spark plugs can fail with age and heat.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.

issues.t: Anti-theft system blocks starting
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or won't crank, and the security light stays on or flashes.
issues.why: The Passlock anti-theft system misreads the ignition and shuts off fuel to the engine. A fault in the ignition switch sensor or the theft-deterrent module is usually behind it.
issues.next: Leave the key in On for about 10 minutes until the security light stops flashing, then try again. If it keeps happening, a shop can test the ignition switch and theft module.

issues.t: Heater fan noisy or speed control acting up
issues.sym: The blower fan squeals or rattles, or only some fan speeds work.
issues.why: The blower motor wears out, and the blower resistor that sets fan speed can fail.
issues.next: Check the cabin air area for leaves first. A worn blower motor or resistor is a simple replacement.

issues.t: Aftermarket replacement ignition switch can slip (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving on a car that has had its ignition switch replaced with an aftermarket part.
issues.why: Some aftermarket replacement ignition switches had the same weak design and could slip from Run to Accessory. Recall 14E-021 covers those parts.
issues.next: If your ignition switch was ever replaced outside the dealer, ask a dealer to check which switch is installed.

issues.t: Fuel feed pipe can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or fuel dripping under the car.
issues.why: On a small batch of 2004 Ions the fuel feed pipe could leak, which is a fire risk. GM recall 04V-281 fixes the pipe.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park outside and check your VIN for open recall 04V-281.
